msg: US Social Security (OASDI) taxable wage base is pinned to a prior-year figure. The Social Security Administration re-announces the base each autumn and the new one applies from 1 January (next reset 2027-01-01).
US elective deferral limit for 401(k)/403(b) is a prior-year figure. The IRS publishes the cost-of-living adjusted limit each autumn and it applies from 1 January (next reset 2027-01-01).

Employer Class 1 secondary National Insurance is still at the 13.8% rate, which applied up to 5 April 2025; the rate rose to 15% from 6 April 2025. UK payroll rates reset at the start of the tax year (next reset 2027-04-06).
The 9100 employer secondary threshold is the 2024-25 figure; it was cut to 5000 from 6 April 2025. UK thresholds reset at the start of the tax year (next reset 2027-04-06).
German Minijob monthly earnings limit is a prior-year figure. The limit is recomputed from the statutory minimum wage and changes on 1 January (next reset 2027-01-01).
Canadian CPP maximum pensionable earnings (YMPE) is a prior-year figure. The Canada Revenue Agency sets the new ceiling every year and it applies from 1 January (next reset 2027-01-01).
French annual social security ceiling (PASS) is a prior-year figure. The ceiling is fixed by decree each year and applies from 1 January (next reset 2027-01-01).
This rate table is keyed to a tax year that has already closed. A table whose newest key is a past year will silently return last year's numbers for this year's payroll run.
A rate block named current/latest/default carries no date, so nothing in the file says which year it holds. Name the block by its effective date instead.
An unresolved TODO/FIXME sits on a statutory figure. A reminder in a comment is not an effective date and will not stop a payroll run.
This rate entry has no effective_from date, so no code and no reader can tell which period the figure belongs to.
This rate entry has no end date, so it will keep being applied after the statutory figure has been replaced.
This rate entry names no country or jurisdiction. Payroll rates reset on different days per country, so an entry without a jurisdiction cannot be checked against any reset date.
This rate entry's own end date is already in the past relative to the run date, so the table is serving a figure it declares expired.
A rate value greater than 1 is stored with no unit key. A consumer that expects a fraction will withhold by a factor of 100, and nothing in the entry says which form is meant.
